name: Family 075, I26+I27+I10 cluster: thermal noisy labels Z = Y + theta (theta ~ K_A), label updates A+ = A + S_p + D_i, and the two-law (true input P vs uniform output U) Fisher-sum identity; provisional N3, F1 (F5 flavour). Slug thermal_labels.
definition: Thermal noisy labels (paper 05-thermal.tex:11-28, 111-158; 06-procedure.tex:72-78, 170-183, 611-630; 09-assembly.tex:159-170). (1) A thermal form on the circle is A(y)=sum_s lambda_s (1 - Re chi_s(y)), lambda_s>=0; q_A(u) = Fourier coefficients of e^{-A}; free energy F(A)=-log q_A(0); K_A = e^{F(A)-A} (a probability density: a centred generalised von Mises / one-site plane-rotator Gibbs density); Delta_A(u)=||1-chi_u||_{L^2(K_A)}; B_A(r)={u: Delta_A(u)<=r}. (2) LABEL: the random input point Y (law P, dP = rho/m_top dU, i.e. sampled proportionally to the input density) is observed through a noisy label Z = Y + theta mod 1 with theta ~ K_A, errors independent given Y; no choice of the procedure ever inspects a sampled label. (3) LABEL UPDATE: on each successful spectral update at interval p the main channel is tightened, A+ = A + S_p + D_i, with spatial form S_p = R_p^2 (1 - Re chi_1), R_p=|p|^{-1}, and a metric form D_i = lambda * (averaged cost over a compressed frequency set) chosen on a flat stretch of free energy; a fresh label of type A+ is drawn. (4) TWO-LAW FISHER SUM: at a live jumping node p of plateau e with post-density a, put M_pm(z) = E_{p_pm}[a(Y) K_A(z-Y)]/alpha_e, M=(M_+ + M_-)/2, D=(M_+ - M_-)/2, J_p = int |D|^2/M dz. Under the TRUE input law, alpha_e/m_p * J_p is exactly the expected squared bias of the next spatial bit of Y given the label Z; bias^2 <= 2 KL(bit || fair) and the entropy chain rule give, summed with UNIFORM output weights, sum_{live jumping p} U(p) alpha_e J_p <= C d (Prop live-budgets (iv)). (5) DECODING: with a^s_p(z) = E_p[a_p(Y) chi_s(Y) r_{j+1}(Y) K_A(z-Y)]/alpha_e and c_A(n) = int chi_n K_A = 1 - Delta_A(n)^2/2 >= 1/2, one has exactly int chi_n(z) a^s_p(z) dz = c_A(n) c_p^{s+n}: a single label-valued moment encodes every modulation s+n with n in the ball B_A(r_sep). Lean (finite version on ZMod 2^M, labels integrated not sampled): Thermal.label, Thermal.channel, Update.next, Procedure.fisher, fisher_bound, duet_decode.
mechanism: To bound a supremum over many linear statistics (characters) of a hidden variable Y, adjoin an auxiliary noisy observation Z = Y + theta whose noise law is shift-invariant with nonnegative Fourier coefficients (a ferromagnetic Gibbs density). Then (a) every statistic chi_{s+n} with n in the noise metric ball is recovered EXACTLY from the Z-conditional moments of chi_s, with multiplicative loss c_A(n) close to 1 (decoding); (b) the per-step squared bias of the filtration given Z is a Fisher information, and its sum along the filtration is bounded by the total relative entropy of Y (chain rule + Pinsker) - one budget regardless of how many statistics are decoded; (c) information is counted under the input-weighted law and transferred to bounds along the uniform/output law by a Radon-Nikodym identity; (d) when too many separated statistics are large, tighten the noise (add terms to the Gibbs energy) and pay with a monovariant (free energy minus log packing number of the metric ball) or with likelihood evidence. In one line: replace a union bound over frequencies by a single noisy side-channel whose Fisher information is paid by entropy and whose positive-definite noise makes a whole ball of frequencies decodable at once.
obstruction: Prop dyadic needs int max_u |sum_j c_p^u eps_j r_{j+2}| <= C d uniformly in the number of modulation frequencies u, where d ~ log ||rho||_inf (the L log L layer height). For ONE fixed frequency the bound is a scalar martingale/entropy estimate: the squared biases of the modulated output bits are paid by the relative entropy of the input density (<= d) via the chain rule. For a supremum over many frequencies the scalar route loses a union-bound/chaining factor that grows with the number of frequencies (log N type losses as in Kolmogorov-Seliverstov-Plessner, Rademacher-Menshov, Bourgain's multi-frequency lemma); every known Carleson proof (Carleson, Fefferman, Lacey-Thiele) instead kills this loss by time-frequency tile combinatorics, which is lossy at the L log L endpoint (best previous: Antonov L log L log log log L). The label converts the problem: information about Y available through Z is a SINGLE budget (the Fisher sum, O(d) by the chain rule, independent of how many frequencies are decoded), and every frequency in a Delta_A-ball around a representative is read off the same label-valued moment with loss factor c_A(n) >= 1/2. Frequencies not yet in the ball force a 'separated high collection', which triggers a label update whose cost is paid either by likelihood evidence (regular update) or by the gap potential F(A) - log|B_A(r)| (cheap update). Thus the cost of choosing frequencies is decoupled from the cost of information (the paper's 'separate costs for information an…
precedent: No earlier equivalent of the full device (noisy label of the input point with ferromagnetic thermal noise, adaptive tightening A+ = A + S_p + D_i, two-law Fisher sum, exact character decoding) was found in harmonic analysis: searches for information-theoretic / noisy-observation proofs of Carleson-type theorems returned only tile-based proofs (Carleson, Fefferman, Lacey-Thiele, Lie, Di Plinio) and the 2026 Lean formalisation of Carleson's theorem. None of them currently uses it; only 083 has a clear Carleson-operator sub-step where it could…
review_grade: N3 provisional (novelty conf 0.35), F1; likely N2
review_verdict: F1-shaped: it adjoins a new auxiliary variable, like an extension variable. Under the strict rule, though, the mechanism is mostly transfer. Stochastic localization with the I-MMSE chain rule, Tao's entropy decrement and Russo–Zou information budgets already say 'pay for many adaptively chosen statistics with one information budget'. The new part is the instantiation in Fourier analysis: ferromagnetic thermal noise makes character decoding exact and independent of the number of frequencies. That reads as a new bridge (N2) unless the speedup test shows it does something those templates cannot. (An earlier Lean caveat is retracted: the fixed ε_j is exactly the instance the paper uses, and the label is on the chain to the comparator.) It has the lowest prior here but the highest value of information, because its downstream test is concrete and would be decisive.
review_test: Bourgain's multi-frequency lemma in a finite model. Lowering its log²N loss toward log N would be a speedup on a different, 35-year-old theorem and would confirm the item. Run the Walsh L log L case first as a cheap check.

name: Pair capacity c_ell(nu)
definition: verbatim paper: Let nu be a probability law with finite support F subset R. For ell in Z, let E_ell(F) be the set of unordered pairs {x,y} subset F satisfying 2^{-ell} <= |x-y| < 2^{1-ell}. Define c_ell(nu) as the maximum of sum_{e in E_ell(F)} w_e subject to w_e >= 0, (1/2) sum_{e containing x} w_e <= nu({x}) (x in F). When E_ell(F) is empty, this maximum is zero. · plain: c_ell(nu) is the largest total mass of fair (equal-weight) two-point laws whose two points lie at a distance in the dyadic band [2^-ell, 2^{1-ell}), subject to their weighted sum being a submeasure of nu. 0 <= c_ell <= 1. Example: nu = p delta_x + (1-p) delta_y has capacity 2 min{p,1-p} in the band containing |x-y|, and 0 in every other band. · equivalent forms: LP form: the fractional b-matching value, with b = 2 nu, of the distance-band graph G_ell(F). Its vertices are F and its edges are the pairs at distance in the band. · Coupling form (elementary, derived here): c_ell(nu) = the maximum mass of a sub-coupling pi <= (nu, nu) supported on ordered pairs with |x-y| in the band. Any sub-coupling can be symmetrised without changing its mass; set w_{xy} = pi(x,y)+pi(y,x). This is exactly how the pair-bound proof deposits mass into the capacity (pairs.tex:182-204; Lean coupling_band_le_capacity). · Dual / Hall form (derived here by max-flow min-cut on the bipartite double cover; not stated in the paper): c_ell(nu) = 1 - max_{A subset F} [ nu(A) - nu(N_ell(A)) ], where N_ell(A) is the set of points at band distance from some point of A. This is a Strassen / defect-Hall type quantity. · lean: FairPairs.capacity nu ell := sSup {t | exists w : nu.edges ell -> R, Feasible w and sum_e w e = t}. capacity_attained proves the sup is a max, by compactness of the feasible polytope.
mechanism: Measure an obstruction by a scale-stratified packing LP: the maximum mass of a measure that can be packed into balanced two-element witnesses whose separation lies in a given dyadic band. Because it is a maximum, any coupling or averaging certificate the proof produces bounds it from below, band by band. Because it is attained, it can be cashed out witness by witness through a local gain lemma whose payoff does not depend on the band. Summing over bands turns information hidden at unknown, arbitrarily fine scales into a scale-free budget. That budget is then played against a bounded telescoping monovariant.
obstruction: Without any separation hypothesis, the exact Shannon entropy of a finite law nu can sit far above its entropy at a grid scale rho. Here nu is the law of translations of n-block composed maps with fixed slope type. The excess may be stored in atoms that are closer together than ANY prescribed scale, even a super-exponential one: Baker 2021 and Barany-Kaenmaki 2021 construct IFSs without exact overlaps whose cylinders condense super-exponentially. Hochman's route needs the hidden information to be visible in a bounded window of scales, which is what exponential separation provides. Varju's Prop 21 converts entropy at ONE scale r into fair-pair mass at that same scale, and only under the single-scale doubling hypothesis H(mu; r/2|r) <= 1.5 H(mu; r|2r). A contradiction argument therefore needs a currency with three properties. (a) It absorbs hidden information from all finer scales at once, without knowing where that information sits; there is no bound on the separating depth J. (b) It can be redeemed scale by scale as entropy gain, with a payoff that does not depend on the scale. (c) It is bounded in each band, so finite band sums stay controlled. c_ell is that currency. Because it is a MAXIMUM, every band-restricted symmetric sub-coupling produced by the randomised-partition averaging is a lower bound for it; this is the deposit side, the pair bound P15. Because it is ATTAINED by an explicit fair-pair packing, each unit can be fed to the two-point gain lemma (Varju Lemma 22 / …
precedent: There is a strong precedent for the definition itself. P14 is N2 bordering on N1, not an N3/F1 eureka step. The analyst grade N2 is confirmed, and there is no case for raising it.
precedent_detail: verdict: There is a strong precedent for the definition itself. P14 is N2 bordering on N1, not an N3/F1 eureka step. The analyst grade N2 is confirmed, and there is no case for raising it. · pre release: Varju, JAMS 2019 (arXiv:1602.00261), Sec. 4.2.3, proof of Prop 21. It takes a decomposition mu = nu + eta_1 + ... + eta_N in which each eta_i is a Bernoulli measure on a pair of points at distance between r/2 and 2r, and ||nu|| is minimal among all such decompositions. Here a "Bernoulli measure" is an equal-weight two-point measure, not normalised. So 1 - min||nu|| is exactly the pair capacity for the single band [r/2, 2r], a ratio-4 band rather than the dyadic ratio-2 band. Varju also mentions a similar decomposition in unpublished Lindenstrauss-Varju work (his ref [17], "work in progress 2018"). He then uses the decomposition across many scale ranges B, together with Prop 20 / Lemma 22, to collect gains (Sec. 4.3). This is the same two-sided pattern: decompose into fair pairs at a scale, then gain from each pair. The 148 paper itself names Prop 21 as a predecessor (pairs.tex:8-9). · Combinatorial optimisation: c_ell is the fractional b-matching number of the distance-band graph (b = 2 nu). Equivalently, it is the maximum mass of a sub-coupling of (nu, nu) on band pairs, or, by max-flow min-cut / defect Hall / a Strassen 1965-type argument, 1 - max_A [nu(A) - nu(N_ell(A))]. These are classical objects. The only new aspects are the stratification into dyadic bands and the use as an entropy currency. · Kittle-Kogler 2025 (arXiv:2501.17795) and Kittle 2021 (arXiv:2103.12684) use scale-local currencies: "variance/trace at scale r" and "detail", with tr(g; 2ar) >> H(g; r|2r). These are linear, non-LP near-neighbours of a scale-indexed pair-mass currency, and they are used to accumulate gains across separated scales. · post release: Kittle-Kogler, The exact overlaps conjecture for self-similar measures on the real line, arXiv:2610.10511, posted Oct 7 2026, one day after the Oct 6 release. They state that GPT-6 Astra found their first proof, which was presented to them on Sept 27 2026. They cite the 148 paper as "independently announced in [20] as paper number 148". They describe their Thm 1.3, sum H(X_i) - H(sum X_i) <= 30 m sum E(X_i), as "a quantitative version of Lemma 3.2 of [20]", with constant C_m = 120 m^2 against O(m^3) for the 148 method. Their currency is the variance energy E(rho) = int_0^infty V_rho(r) dr/r, where V_rho(r) is the normalised local variance in intervals of length r. The proof uses Poisson point-process cuts and Margulis-Russo formulas, and the words "pair" and "fair" do not occur. So another model found the pair-bound MECHANISM (random cuts plus a scale-free fine-scale currency) independently, and it was reused immediately. The DEFINITION c_ell, however, was replaced by a linear functional. This is evidence that c_ell is replaceable and is not the indispensable eureka object. · No other post-release use of "pair capacity" w…

name: Thompson's group F is nonamenable · Recursive coloring
definition: setting: H a real Hilbert space, B its closed unit ball, f:B->B L-Lipschitz with ||f(x)-x|| >= delta > 0 for all x (Benyamini-Sternfeld; the paper builds one on L^2([0,1];R^2) with delta = 1/2). D >= 2 with D > 4L^2/delta^2. Internal basic dyadic intervals I_1 < ... < I_D (paper: I_j = [(2j-1)2^-r, 2j 2^-r] with 2^r > 2D; Lean: depth 2D, index 2i+1). For a basic dyadic partition T that respects I, T_I = { s_I^{-1}(K) : K in T, K subset I } is its normalized restriction (s_I : [0,1] -> I the increasing affine chart). · recursion: p(T) = f( (1/D) * sum_{j=1..D} p(T_{I_j}) ) if T respects every I_j; p(T) = 0 otherwise. Well founded on the number of cells, since each I_j is internal, so T_{I_j} has fewer cells. p(T) is in B. · pullback: Family I = {I_i} union {I_i . I_j} (parents and descendants, I.J = s_I(J)). (n,g) is admissible if gT^(n) is basic and respects every member of I. X_I^(n)(g) = p((gT^(n))_I) if admissible, else 0. Scalar correlations phi_{I,J}(g) = <X_I(g), X_J(g)> lie in [-1,1]. · key identities: (T_I)_J = T_{I.J} (restriction composes) · exact covariance: if h maps I affinely onto I', then ((hg)T^(n))_{I'} = (gT^(n))_I · recursive identity on admissible g: X_{I_i}(g) = f(z_i(g)), z_i = (1/D) sum_j X_{I_i.I_j}(g), m = (1/D) sum_k X_{I_k}(g) = (1/D) sum_i f(z_i) · worked example: p(T^(0)) = 0, p(T^(r)) = f(0), p(T^(2r)) = f(f(0)): on uniform partitions the coloring iterates f, so it behaves like a bounded 'depth counter' that never stabilises.
mechanism: Setting: a group acts on 'configurations' that can be refined to be fine at every scale, and that carry a self-similar restriction operator (sub-configuration on a cell, renormalised to the whole). Colour each configuration recursively by a vector in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert ball: a configuration's colour is a fixed Lipschitz self-map f, with no approximate fixed point, applied to the mean of the colours of its restrictions to D fixed separated cells. The colour is bounded, unlike depth, and cannot settle at a fixed point, unlike any finite-dimensional colour. If the group has a fixed finite set of elements that carry any separated pair of cells, at any scales, onto one reference pair, then an approximately invariant finite average makes all pair correlations nearly equal. Pair-exchangeability concentrates the child-means near the parent-mean, so the recursion forces an approximate fixed point of f, a contradiction. In short: 'recursively aggregate a vector-valued colouring through a map with no approximate fixed points, so approximate invariance forces a contradiction'. Abstract applicability conditions: (a) self-similar restriction with (T_I)_J = T_{I.J}; (b) a well-founded measure decreasing under restriction; (c) configurations that can be made simultaneously fine on any finite cell family for any finite set of group elements, i.e. the orbit map g -> gT^(n) at a level n chosen after A; (d) a FIXED finite set of scale-changing transports for every separated pair, with exact covariance. (c) and (d) are where it fails for amenable groups: translation-only groups such as IET or polygon exchanges fail (d); level-preserving tree-automorphism groups fail (d); and actions on finite point configurations, such as F acting on k-subsets of dyadics, whose finite-set stabilisers are co-amenable, fail (c).
obstruction: Approximate invariance (Folner) gives control only over AVERAGES of BOUNDED functions, with error eta*||phi||_inf. The natural invariant that should rule out Folner sets in F is unbounded and well-founded: depth or cell count strictly decreases under restriction to a parent (T_{I_1.I_1} has fewer cells than T_{I_1}), while transports equate the laws of restrictions at different scales. With a bounded scalar surrogate the averaging works, but every bounded scalar or finite-dimensional recursion has a fixed point (Brouwer), so it can stabilise and give no contradiction. That is why Moore's scalar tree colourings and Akhmedov's integer height function did not close the problem, and why Moore's Folner-function recursion only yields tower-type size bounds. A second obstruction is that the recursion is nonlinear: E f(z) != f(E z), so first-moment invariance is useless. The device removes both at once. (1) Bounded but non-stabilising: p takes values in the unit ball, yet the recursion goes through a Lipschitz f with no approximate fixed point, which exists only in infinite dimension. It is a bounded, Lipschitz replacement for 'height + 1'. (2) The nonlinearity is handled by second moments only. Approximate invariance under a FIXED finite set S of pair transports makes all separated-pair correlations approximately equal (alpha +- eta). Averaging D exchangeable vectors then concentrates z_i near m (variance <= 4/D + 4eta). Lipschitz continuity gives f(z_i) ~ f(m), so m = mean f(z_i) …

The combination (recursive tree/partition colouring) + (vector values in an infinite-dimensional ball) + (Lipschitz map with no approximate fixed point) + (pair-exchangeability concentration) does not appear in the literature I could reach. · nearest neighbours: Moore 2013, Ramsey characterisation: finite SCALAR colourings of finite binary trees with a convex Ramsey property. Neither recursive nor vector-valued; it is a reformulation, not a contradiction mechanism. · Moore, 'Fast growth in the Folner function for Thompson's group F' (arXiv:0905.1118): recursion over restrictions giving tower lower bounds on Folner sets. Scalar and unbounded, so it yields size bounds and no contradiction. This is the closest in spirit: the device is the bounded, non-stabilising upgrade of this recursion. · Akhmedov, height-function criteria (arXiv:0902.4755, 1310.4395): unbounded integer-valued heights. The device replaces 'height' by a bounded Lipschitz Hilbert-valued counter. · Monod 2013/2023: explicit fixed-point-free AFFINE convex compact spaces for H(A); by Monod's own statement the criterion fails precisely for F. · Day 1961, Gheysens-Monod 2017, Barroso-Mbombo-Pestov (arXiv:1410.8370): affine fixed-point characterisations. No nonlinear map, no recursion. · Benyamini-Sternfeld 1983 and Lin-Sternfeld 1985: the map itself, with no group-theoretic use. · Jones / Brothier-Jones Pythagorean representations: recursive assignment of Hilbert vectors along trees through a fixed LINEAR isometry. These are representations, not contradictions, and they have no averaging or fixed-point-free map. A structural cousin only. · Diaconis-Freedman finite de Finetti: the concentration step (EC2), not the definition. · post release use: None found as of 2026-10-09. Sources checked: VibeMathed problem page (lists the result as 'Candidate (review pending)'); Gil Kalai's blog of 2026-10-07 (mentions the claim, no assessment); press coverage of the release; arXiv searches for Benyamini-Sternfeld plus amenability; 'A Human Audit of OpenAI's AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs' arXiv:2608.14673 (covers the August release, not this item); arXiv:2609.25931 (Lipschitz group actions, unrelated). · caveats: The underlying theorem is unreviewed. review_verdict: The closest match in the corpus to the extension-variable profile. The colour p(T) is a defined object that is absent from the statement and exists only to drive the proof. It dissolves a real obstruction: Følner sets control only averages of bounded functions, while the natural invariant (depth) is unbounded, so the proof needs a bounded invariant that never stabilises. Its ingredient, the Benyamini–Sternfeld map, is transfer (N0). The coupling to F's self-similarity has no precedent found, and six earlier claimed proofs never used a vector-valued recursive invariant, so it looks hard to construct. Two things stand between this and a confirmed jump. (a) The proof is unrefereed and the Lean has not been built; if the proof is wrong the item is void. (b) The strict definition needs speedups on OTHER theorems, and the definition's own reach looks narrow: groups that contain F inherit nonamenability from the theorem, not from the device, so they test nothing. It may be a one-problem key rather than a jump.
review_test: Re-run the device directly on Farey or n-adic cells for Monod's H(A) and Lodha–Moore G_0, without embedding F, and derive an explicit Kesten-norm bound for F. Negative controls must fail: the amenable IET subgroups and family 253's polygon-exchange group.

name: Spliced stable permutation symbol F_pi(x,y) = prod_i (x_i + y_{pi(i)})
definition: symbol: For a permutation pi of a finite set V, F_pi(x,y) := prod_{i in V} (x_i + y_{pi(i)}), a multiaffine polynomial in 2|V| variables (one input variable x_i and one output variable y_j per point). For a random pi, the law symbol is E F_pi. · stability lemma: If pi is a finite product of independent Bernoulli(u) transpositions and deterministic permutations (or a limit of such laws: finite-time Poisson exchange processes, uniform permutations on subsets, and independent products of these), then E F_pi is stable, i.e. it has no zero when every variable lies in the open upper half-plane. Proof: the identity symbol is a product of nonvanishing factors; composing with a Bernoulli transposition is the partial symmetrization (1-u)F + u tauF in two output variables, which preserves stability (BBL Thm 4.20; the paper gives an elementary two-variable section proof); limits by Hurwitz. · layering: Cut the periodic time circle of Toth's exchange picture at every pin time; V = disjoint union of slot layers at the cuts; the layer-to-layer maps are independent, so the layered symbol F_V = E prod_{i in V}(x_i + y_{pi(i)}) is a product of stable interval symbols, hence stable. · splicing: Eliminate an unpinned vertex q by setting x_q = y_q = t and extracting the coefficient of t. On a path i -> q -> j the factors (x_i + t)(t + y_j) give x_i + y_j (the path is spliced); on a fixed point the factor x_q + y_q = 2t gives the factor 2. Removing all non-pins gives F_P(x,y) = E_b[ 2^{n_P(pi)} prod_{i in P}(x_i + y_{sigma(i)}) ], where sigma is the next-pin permutation and n_P is the number of cycles missing P. Each closed cycle that avoids the pins contributes exactly the Heisenberg (Toth) cycle weight 2 = dim C^2, so the spliced symbol encodes the PINNED, CYCLE-WEIGHTED law P_P, with no stability lost (identification and differentiation are closure operations). · output extraction: G_T(y) = E_P prod_{i in T} y_{sigma(i)} = Z_P^{-1} (prod_{i in P\T} d/dx_i) F_P |_{x=0} is the stable subset generating polynomial of sigma(T); stability gives P_P(J subset sigma(T)) <= prod_j P_P(j in sigma(T)) (BBL Thm 4.9 consequence). · decisive use: Proposition prop:pin-test: P_E(T subset B_E) <= (2r)^{|T|}, where B_E is the union of cycles avoiding the pin set E and r is the mean return fraction. The factor 2^{|T|} comes from comparing pin laws P_E and P_{E u T}. · companion variant: The spherical-law companion (Oct 5) uses the disk form E prod_i (1 + x_i y_{pi(i)}), zero-free on |x_i|,|y_i…
mechanism: Encode a random bijection by its 'two-sided symbol' prod_i (in_i + out_{pi(i)}), which is a stability-preserving (real-stable) object under independent local mixing moves. Compose independent layers by multiplying symbols in disjoint variables, then take a trace by contracting each output variable with the matching input variable (identify and extract the linear coefficient). The contraction is a stability-preserving closure operation that splices paths and assigns every closed loop a fixed weight equal to the trace of the identity on a 2-dimensional space (here 2). The result is a stable generating polynomial for a GLOBALLY loop-weighted measure, from which negative dependence (product bounds on simultaneous positive events) follows. Field-independently: 'a loop-weighted measure whose loop weight equals tr(I) on a two-state space is a contraction (partial trace) of a product of stable local transfer symbols, so it inherits negative dependence from the local moves.' Equivalently (precedent view): the law symbol is the Borcea-Branden symbol T[prod(z_i + w_i)] of the permutation-averaging operator, and splicing is the half-plane form of an Asano contraction, i.e. a stable-polynomial transfer-matrix trace.
obstruction: The cycle-weighted interchange measure (weight theta^{#cycles}, theta = 2 for Toth's Heisenberg representation) has no known negative-dependence / strongly Rayleigh structure: BBL-type stability is known for unweighted symmetric exclusion and interchange (theta = 1), and the weight 2^{#cycles} is a global, non-local reweighting that partial symmetrization does not see. The model's preceding route (holes + exterior powers, determinants/signed minors) computes first moments but cannot bound the POSITIVE event that many test points simultaneously lie on cycles avoiding the pins (trace conflict C9). Without a positivity-preserving encoding, one cannot get a product bound (2r)^m for the simultaneous event, and density/scalar bootstrap arguments are defeated by trapping walls and arbitrary phase fractions (C7, C8). The spliced symbol solves both: it carries a positivity-preserving (stable) encoding through the unweighted exchange layers where BBL applies, and the splicing contraction itself manufactures the factor 2 per closed cycle, so the weighted pinned law inherits stability.

name: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension · Character classes
definition: Setting: G = Z_p acts faithfully, orientation-preservingly on W = O x R^{d-n} (O a connected invariant chart subset of R^n, d odd >= 3, d > n). c: S^d -> W^+ collapses S^d \ W to infinity, q: W^+ -> Y = W^+/G, and t: Y -> X is a 'compact test' (X a compact test space, b_t = t(q(infinity)) with a basis of contractible neighbourhoods). Put f_t = t q c, A_t = R f_{t*} C_{S^d} (C = R^2 with B(z,w) = Re(z wbar)), alpha_t: A_t -> D_{X,d} A_t the pushed-forward orientation form; [A_t, alpha_t] lies in E_d(X) = W_d(T(X)), the triangular Witt group of the test category T(X) (thick subcategory of D^b(Sh_R(X)) generated by Rf_* R_B for arbitrary continuous f from compact polyhedra B). Off b_t, A_t is the pushforward of the orbit sheaf H = q_* C, which splits by characters Lambda = mu_{p^infty}: H = (+)_lambda H_lambda, H_lambda = ker(T - M_lambda). A finite partition Lambda = D_0 u ... u D_{m-1} gives projectors that are orthogonal and self-adjoint on A_t|_{X \ b_t} (Lemma orthogonality), hence, via the germ theorem, endomorphisms e_i of A_t in the Verdier quotient Q_U(X) = T(X)/T(U) for a contractible open U containing b_t, with e_i e_j = delta_ij e_i, sum e_i = 1, e_i^dagger = e_i. DEFINITION (06-character-classes.tex:225-235): z_i(t) in E_d(X) is the unique class with l_U(z_i(t)) = [A_t, alpha_t] + [A_t, alpha_t o (2 e_i - id)] in W_d(Q_U(X)), where l_U: E_d(X) -> W_d(Q_U(X)) is the integral localization isomorphism (valid because U is contractible and d is odd). No image object of e_i is formed; if e_i did split orthogonally, the right side would be 2 times the Witt class of the e_i-summand. Proved properties: independent of U; sum_i z_i(t) = 2 [A_t, alpha_t] integrally (explicit isometry S = sum_j E_j P_j, S^2 = 1, S^dagger Q_0 S = Q); covariant g_* z_i(t) = z_i(g t); homotopy invariant in t (close-pair space C_d); and for a test h concentrated on a region V of p^k labelled sheets, multiplication by the sheet multiplier beta conjugates e_i to e_{i-1}, so z_0(h) = ... = z_{m-1}(h). Used with I49: fix the lattice L_d^{-1} Z u_d first, then for m = p^k > 4 L_d the m integral classes z_i(a) have equal rational images summing to 4 u_d, so each is (4/m) u_d, outside the lattice.
mechanism: Given a self-dual object whose symmetry splits it into many parts only generically (off a small 'bad' locus), assign each part an integral class without ever splitting off the part. Take the form plus the same form twisted by the reflection 2e-1, which equals twice the part's class. Then lift it from the localized category (bad locus killed) back to the global integral group, using an isomorphism that holds because the bad locus is contractible. The parts sum to a fixed integral total and a cyclic symmetry permutes them, so each part equals total/m. With denominators bounded a priori by a lattice fixed before m, m = p^k large gives a contradiction. In short: integral 'isotypic signatures' for a profinite symmetry, defined by reflection-twisting and localization-lifting, defeat the fractional Haar measure of the parts.
obstruction: A faithful Z_p-action should be ruled out by a 'Haar fraction' argument: the action spreads a degree-one class equally over p^k character parts for every k, so each part carries 1/p^k of it. Classically this needs an integer-valued invariant for each part, and three things block it. (1) Wild orbit spaces. Y = W/G has cohomological dimension n+2 (Yang) and non-finitely-generated cohomology, so Euler-characteristic, transfer or Smith-theory counts on Y give no integers. (2) Splitting needs dividing. Isotypic decompositions split ordinary (co)homology only after inverting |G| (here infinite) or tensoring with C. Complex-coefficient homology loses integrality: the character parts of H_*(.;C) are just vector spaces, with no lattice to violate. (3) The bad point. The character decomposition of the orbit sheaf exists only away from b = t(y_inf), the image of the point at infinity and of the non-free orbits collapsed there. The projectors do not extend to direct summands of A_t over b, and the stalks are infinite-dimensional, so one cannot form 'the e_i-part' as an object of a category with a Witt group. The device dissolves all three. Real coefficients plus Witt groups give integrality, since signatures are integers and Witt classes are integral before tensoring with Q. The 'twice the summand' form [A, alpha] + [A, alpha(2e-1)] needs only a self-adjoint idempotent on the existing object, not its image.
